name: Tools the team uses to support customers

failureModes.prompt: Should every change a staff member makes to a customer's account be recorded with who made it?
failureModes.why: without a record, a mistaken or improper change by staff cannot be traced, explained or reversed

options.label: Record who did what, and when
options.consequence: a little storage, and every staff change can be explained later

options.label: Keep no record
options.consequence: less to build, and a wrong change cannot be traced to anyone

failureModes.recommended: Record who did what, and when
failureModes.provenBy: a test that performs a staff action and asserts a record names the staff member, the customer, the change and the time

failureModes.prompt: Should the admin pages check for a staff sign-in on every request, or rely on the address staying private?
failureModes.why: a hidden address can appear in shared links, screenshots or search results, and then anyone who finds it can act as staff

options.label: Check staff sign-in every time
options.consequence: a little more work, and a known address shows nothing to outsiders

options.label: Rely on the address staying private
options.consequence: quicker to build, and anyone who finds the address can act as staff

failureModes.provenBy: a test that requests each admin page without a staff sign-in and asserts the server refuses it

failureModes.prompt: When staff change a customer's account, should the same rules apply as when the customer does it?
failureModes.why: editing the database directly skips the product's own checks, such as limits, billing and messages to the customer

options.label: Same rules, through the same server code
options.consequence: slower to add admin actions, and staff cannot create states the product was not built for

options.label: Staff edit the database directly
options.consequence: fastest for staff, and one edit can break an account in ways nobody planned for

failureModes.recommended: Same rules, through the same server code
failureModes.provenBy: a test that makes one change through the admin tool and asserts the same limits, billing updates and customer messages as the customer's own path

failureModes.prompt: When staff view the product as a customer, should they give a reason that is recorded?
failureModes.why: viewing as a customer shows their private data, and a recorded reason lets every viewing be checked later

options.label: Require a reason and record it
options.consequence: one more step for staff, and each viewing can be accounted for

options.label: Let staff view freely
options.consequence: quicker support, and private data can be browsed with no trace

failureModes.recommended: Require a reason and record it
failureModes.provenBy: a test that starts viewing as a customer without a reason and asserts it is refused, and that a viewing with a reason is recorded

failureModes.prompt: While viewing as a customer, should staff be able to make changes or only look?
failureModes.why: changes made while viewing as a customer look as if the customer made them unless they are marked

options.label: Only look
options.consequence: safer, and staff ask the customer to make changes themselves

options.label: Make changes, marked as staff
options.consequence: faster support, and every change needs a staff mark in the record

failureModes.provenBy: a test that tries to change data while viewing as a customer and asserts the chosen behaviour, refused or recorded as staff

failureModes.prompt: Should support staff see only the customer details their task needs?
failureModes.why: if every support login can read everything, a stolen login can then expose the private data of every customer

options.label: Only what each task needs
options.consequence: more roles to set up, and a stolen staff login exposes less

options.label: Everything about every customer
options.consequence: simpler, and every support login can read all private data

failureModes.provenBy: a test that signs in with the support role and asserts fields outside its tasks, such as payment details, are not returned
